tests.purpose: An insertion inside a feature grows it, marks the document modified, and undo/redo restore the exact record. Inserting exactly at a feature's first base shifts it; inserting right after its last base leaves it alone; in both cases it covers the same bases. Deleting all bases of a (complement join) feature removes it; a partial delete keeps it; undo restores location and qualifiers; redo/undo is stable. Replace = delete then insert at start: new bases join the feature only when the replaced stretch is strictly inside; at the start/end they stay outside; replacing all of it removes it. For a two-part join, insertions in the gap or at part boundaries grow the gap, insertions inside a part grow that part, and a delete across the gap trims both parts. A join and a complement(join) keep their own sequence and part order through outside edits, and reverse-complementing mirrors their parts and flips the strand.
